items.title: Telangana orders statewide probe into illegal human egg harvesting racket
items.summary: Telangana Health Minister C Damodar Rajanarasimha has ordered a detailed investigation into the alleged illegal harvesting and commercial sale of human eggs in the state, following the arrest of eight people in Hyderabad on October 30. Police also rescued 43 women during the operation. The Minister instructed health officials to identify those involved and initiate strict action against institutions and individuals violating the law. Subsequently, task force teams stepped up inspections of in-vitro fertilisation (IVF) centres across Telangana. Authorities have inspected 27 of the 44 registered assisted reproductive technology (ART) facilities in the state. The inspections revealed 13 violations across seven hospitals, prompting officials to issue show-cause notices to the managements. Checks at the remaining facilities are continuing. The health department is also examining documents seized by the police and seeking information from the National Assisted Reproductive Technology and Surrogacy Registry. items.title: Marico elevates Bony Rai as Head - Legal
items.summary: Marico Limited has elevated Bony Rai to the position of Head - Legal. Rai is a 2017 graduate of Nalanda Law College. He is a member of The Institute of Company Secretaries of India. Rai has been with Marico for the past six years, having joined as an Assistant Company Secretary in 2020. With over 13 years of experience, his expertise lies in corporate law, FMCG and Retail regulations, mergers & acquisitions, advisory and cross-border transactions, and corporate governance. As a legal counsel and company secretary, he navigates the complexities of FMCG regulations, retail operations, and international business structures, ensuring compliance while enabling growth. Aside from his time at Marico, Rai has previously been engaged at Reliance Industries and Onward Technologies. items.title: Possibility of crime no ground to restrict operating hours of licensed bars: Kerala High Court
items.summary: The Kerala High Court on Tuesday held that the Police cannot impose restrictions on the timings of DJ parties conducted by establishments with appropriate liquor licences (FL-3 permits) that allow their operation during extended hours [ Mahadevan v State of Kerala & ors ]. Justice Murali Purushothaman opined that the mere possibility of criminal activities is no ground to impose restrictions on the operation of such facilities. " The mere possibility of criminal activities cannot, by itself, constitute sufficient justification for imposing restrictions under the Kerala Police Act on the extended operating hours of the FL-3 hotel permitted under the Foreign Liquor (Amendment) Rules, 2026" the Court said. The Court held that while the Police have a responsibility to curb crime, it cannot restrict the activities of licenced bars by merely citing suspicions of criminal activities like drug use at such premises, unless rules restricting such bar timings are put in place by the State. items.title: HC directs Tamil Nadu govt to file district-wise report on SC/ST Act implementation
items.summary: The Madurai Bench of the Madras High Court has directed the Tamil Nadu government and the Director General of Police (DGP) to file a comprehensive, district-wise statistical report on the implementation of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act in the last five years. The report is to be submitted to the court on November 24. The court was hearing a plea filed by Kathir, the founder-director of the Madurai-based rights organisation, Evidence. Most notably, the High Court has demanded details of the total number of cases registered under the Act and the number of cases in which investigation has been completed in each district. items.title: Karnataka Muslim group flags alleged disproportionate deletion of Muslim voters during SIR
items.summary: The Karnataka Rajya Muslim Okkoota (KRMO) has questioned the deletion of voters during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. It has sought an explanation from the Election Commission of India (ECI), citing data that shows Muslims were disproportionately represented in certain deletion categories. In a statement on Monday, November 9, the organisation said an analysis of booth-level data published by the ECI, conducted by political research consultancy Sankalp, found that 27.59% of voters had been deleted across the 10 Assembly constituencies represented by Muslim MLAs. This was higher than the statewide deletion rate of 19.45%. The 10 constituencies had 9,62,359 Muslim voters on the 2025 electoral rolls. Of these, 2,46,759, or 25.64%, were deleted during the revision. The overall deletion rate in these constituencies was 27.59%, while the rate among voters from other communities was 28.79%. The analysis also found that more than 8.80 lakh Muslim voters were deleted across 64 constituencies where Muslims account for at least 15% of the electorate. items.title: Cybercriminals siphon Rs 22.3 cr from Tamil Nadu rural healthcare funds
items.summary: Cybercriminals allegedly siphoned off Rs 22.30 crore from a bank account maintained by Tamil Nadu’s Rural Development and Panchayat Raj Department. The money, allocated for rural healthcare infrastructure, was transferred through 46 unauthorised transactions using the department’s online banking system. The fraud came to light after KR Ramprasad, a Block Development Officer and Superintendent attached to the Directorate of Rural Development and Panchayat Raj, lodged a complaint with the Chennai Police Commissioner. According to the complaint, Rs 22,30,04,879 was transferred from the department’s Single Nodal Account with HDFC Bank’s CIT Nagar branch between October 12 and 30. The account, held in the name of the Director of Rural Development and Panchayat Raj, contained funds released by the Union and Tamil Nadu governments under the Fifteenth Finance Commission’s Health Sector Grants. The grants, covering the period from 2021-22 to 2025-26, are intended to strengthen primary healthcare infrastructure and services in rural areas through Rural Local Bodies.
